However, no comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the aforesaid notices published in the newspapers by the Petitioner. 6. The Petitioner is allowed to recover the fee paid for filing the Petition and publication expenses incurred on this count directly from the beneficiaries or long-term customers, as the case may be, in terms of Regulation 94(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 107. MPPMCL, vide affidavit dated 9.12.2025, has submitted that contentions of the Petitioner regarding security expenses, consequential IOWC, insurance expense and capital cost are premature and unwarranted, as the 2019 Tariff Regulations for the 201924 and 2024 Tariff Regulations for the 2024-29 tariff period do not allow the same. Furthermore, the Petitioner has filed Petition No. 45/MP/2024 before the Commission for recovery of capital spares and IOWC. The Petitioner should not be allowed to seek any claims from the Commission which are not included in the instant Petition. Therefore, the Petitioner’s request for filing a separate Petition for claiming capital spares is infructuous and is denied, as the same is already _sub-judice_ before the Commission in Petition No 45/MP/2024. a) The details of AFC claimed by the Petitioner in the instant Petition and the trued-up AFC approved in the instant order with respect to the Asset-I for the 2019- 116.
